name: InterContinental Jordan
positioning: Five-star city hotel on one of Amman's seven hills (officially InterContinental Amman (Jordan)), with a large rooftop terrace and a spa with indoor and outdoor pools
best_for: Travelers who want a hilltop base in Amman near the Old City and the Citadel
Guests who want a spa with an indoor pool, sauna and steam rooms in the city

facts.text: The hotel is perched atop one of Amman's seven hills, in the heart of Jordan's capital.
The hotel is in the Diplomatic Area, not far from the Old City and the Citadel.
The hotel has the city's largest rooftop terrace.
SPA InterContinental has a heated indoor pool, jacuzzi, sauna and steam rooms.
SPA InterContinental offers treatments from massages and facials to holistic therapies.
The hotel has an outdoor pool with sunbeds, described as a retreat away from the city buzz.
Premium Rooms may include a city view and a walk-in shower.
Suites include Junior Suites, Presidential Suites and a Royal Suite, which may be on a high floor.
Large public areas with seating provide impromptu meeting space.
The hotel's restaurants serve Indian, Mexican, Japanese, international and Lebanese cuisine.
Burj Al Hamam serves Lebanese home cooking and daily fresh seafood, with dishes such as Kibbeh Nayeh and Shanklish.
The hotel holds Green Key sustainability certification.

highlights.text: The hotel sits atop one of Amman's seven hills and has the city's largest rooftop terrace.
SPA InterContinental pairs a heated indoor pool, jacuzzi, sauna and steam rooms with massages, facials and holistic therapies.
Rooms are large, with attention to detail, particularly in the bathrooms.
Breakfast is served in the Atrium, near the main lobby, under a glass ceiling that showcases Amman skies.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes the urban setting may lack a resort-style ambiance.
Golf is off-site: the 9-hole Bisharat Golf Course is south of Amman.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
